module callbacks
  /// Task-safe application dependencies captured by request handlers.
  ///
  /// The repository is a host resource handle. Its Host API schema declares
  /// `database.Connection` task-safe, which is what lets this whole struct be
  /// captured by a closure that crosses into a task.
  export struct App
    field repository: database.Connection
    field metrics: Shared<Metrics>
  /// A booking this service stored.
  export struct Booking
    field id: String
  /// Something a request did that subscribers may care about.
  export enum Event
    case BookingCreated(String)
  /// Immutable event subscriptions shared by request tasks.
  export struct EventBus
    field subscribers: Map<String, Array<EventHandler>>
  /// A callback stored by the event bus.
  export type EventHandler = async fn(event: Event) -> Result<Unit, Error>
  /// A callback stored by the router and invoked for each request.
  export type Handler = async fn(request: http.Request) -> Result<http.Response, Error>
  /// Mutable counters shared across request tasks.
  export struct Metrics
    field requests: Int
    field failures: Int
  /// Immutable routes shared by all request tasks.
  export struct Router
    field routes: Array<http.Route>
  /// Runs a server with immutable routes and structured background work.
  export async fn main() -> Result<Unit, Error>
    requires clock, console, database, http
    capability-open

module codegen
  /// Builds the `httpstatus.StatusCode` module from `files/status_codes.txt`,
  /// which pairs each numeric code with a `PascalCase` case name as
  /// alternating whitespace-separated tokens: `200 Ok 404 NotFound ...`. One
  /// data file driving both the enum's cases and its `code()` accessor is what
  /// keeps them from drifting apart the way two hand-written lists would.
  export fn statusCodes() -> Result<String, Error>
    requires files

module config
  /// Validated application configuration.
  export struct Config
    field port: Int
    field logLevel: LogLevel
  /// Configuration validation failures.
  export enum ConfigError
    case InvalidPort(String)
    case InvalidLogLevel(String)
  /// Supported logging levels.
  export enum LogLevel
    case Debug
    case Info
    case Warn
    case Error
  /// Loads configuration from the host environment.
  export fn loadConfig() -> Result<Config, ConfigError>
    requires env

module cq
  /// Runs one transformation over one file.
  ///
  /// Everything a run needs is decided before a byte is read: which
  /// transformation, which file, which format, and where the output goes. What
  /// happens after that is one loop that never holds more than one record.
  export fn main() -> Result<Unit, Error>
    requires console, files, process
    capability-open
  /// Writes a deterministic sample of bookings, for measuring.
  ///
  /// The large input this example's numbers were taken over is not checked in --
  /// a hundred thousand records is fifteen megabytes, and a repository is a bad
  /// place to keep one. It is generated instead, by this, from a seed, so the
  /// file two people measure over is the same file.
  ///
  /// The writer is the same `files.Writer` the transformations write through, so
  /// generating the input is itself a streaming job: this holds one record at a
  /// time exactly as `cq` does.
  export fn sample() -> Result<Unit, Error>
    requires console, files, process

module cq.csv
  /// Renders `fields` as one CSV line, without its terminator.
  export fn formatRecord(fields: Array<String>) -> String
  /// Splits one CSV line into its fields.
  ///
  /// The rules are RFC 4180's, with one deliberate exception. A field may be
  /// quoted with `"`, a quoted field may contain commas, and `""` inside a
  /// quoted field is one literal quote. An unquoted field is taken exactly as
  /// written, including any spaces around it: trimming would be this program
  /// deciding that a value the input chose to include was not meant.
  ///
  /// The exception is that a record may not span lines. RFC 4180 lets a quoted
  /// field contain a newline, and the reader upstream of this hands over one
  /// line at a time, so a quoted field that is still open when the line ends is
  /// reported rather than continued. Making it work means the reader and the
  /// splitter having to agree about quoting, which is the format leaking into
  /// the layer whose whole job is not to know about it.
  export fn splitRecord(line: String) -> Result<Array<String>, Detail>

module cq.diag
  /// Where in one line something went wrong, and what.
  ///
  /// A parser knows the column and not the line: it is handed one record at a
  /// time and has no idea which. `locate` is what supplies the rest, at the one
  /// place in the program that is counting.
  export struct Detail
    field column: Int
    field message: String
  /// A detail, once the record it came from is known.
  export struct Diagnostic
    field source: String
    field line: Int
    field column: Int
    field message: String
  /// Reports `diagnostic` the way a compiler reports one, so an editor that
  /// already knows how to jump to `file:line:column` can jump to a bad record.
  export fn describe(diagnostic: Diagnostic) -> String
  /// Places `detail` at line `line` of `source`.
  export fn locate(detail: Detail, source: String, line: Int) -> Diagnostic

module cq.json
  /// A JSON value.
  ///
  /// JSON has one number type, so this does too: an integer that arrived in the
  /// input is a `Number` like any other, and a program that needs an `Int` asks
  /// for one at the point where it knows that is what the field means. Putting
  /// the distinction here instead would be inventing a JSON that the format does
  /// not have.
  export enum Json
    case Null
    case Bool(Bool)
    case Number(Float)
    case Text(String)
    case Items(Array<Json>)
    case Fields(Map<String, Json>)
  /// The field `name` of an object, or `None` for anything else.
  ///
  /// A value that is not an object has no fields rather than an empty set of
  /// them, and both answer `None` here; a caller that needs to tell the two
  /// apart matches on the value itself.
  export fn field(value: Json, name: String) -> Option<Json>
  /// Parses `text` as one complete JSON value.
  ///
  /// The whole of `text` must be that value: trailing content is an error rather
  /// than something the caller is left to notice, because a line of JSON Lines
  /// that has more after the record is not a record with a comment on it.
  export fn parse(text: String) -> Result<Json, Detail>
  /// Renders `value` as JSON on one line, which is what a JSON Lines record is.
  ///
  /// Object fields come out in `Map` order, which is ascending by key, so two
  /// runs over the same input write the same bytes.
  export fn render(value: Json) -> String

module cq.pipeline
  /// What one run did.
  ///
  /// Three counts and nothing else. A run over a hundred thousand records has a
  /// hundred thousand chances to be told something, and a report that kept them
  /// would be the thing this program exists not to do; each diagnostic is
  /// written when it happens and only the tally outlives it.
  ///
  /// `read` counts the records that folded and `skipped` the ones that did not,
  /// so the two together are how many were taken from the input -- which is what
  /// `--limit` bounds.
  export struct Outcome
    field read: Int
    field written: Int
    field skipped: Int
  /// Where a run's output goes.
  ///
  /// The console is not a file this host can open -- `files` is rooted, and a
  /// terminal has no path inside any root -- so writing to one and writing to
  /// the other are two different Host APIs, and this is the one place in the
  /// program that knows which is in use.
  export enum Sink
    case Console
    case File(files.Writer)
  /// Reads every record of `reader`, folds it, and writes what comes back.
  ///
  /// The loop holds one line, one step's rows, and the transformation's own
  /// state. Nothing accumulates that the transformation did not choose to
  /// accumulate, which is what makes the memory a run holds a property of the
  /// program rather than of the file.
  ///
  /// A record that cannot be read stops the run, unless `skipInvalid`, in which
  /// case it is reported and counted and the next record is read. Stopping is
  /// the default because a summary computed from most of the input is a wrong
  /// answer that looks like a right one.
  export fn transform<S>(reader: files.Reader, sink: Sink, source: String, format: Format, columns: Array<String>, initial: S, step: fn(state: S, line: String, number: Int) -> Result<Step<S>, Detail>, finish: fn(state: S) -> Array<Array<Cell>>, skipInvalid: Bool, limit: Option<Int>) -> Result<Outcome, Error>
    requires console
    capability-open

module cq.programs
  /// What the confirmed-bookings transformation carries between records.
  ///
  /// Nothing, and the type says so. This program writes as it reads, one row per
  /// record it keeps, so no part of the input outlives the line it arrived on.
  export struct NoState
    field kept: Int
  /// Which transformation a run performs.
  ///
  /// A program is a case of an enum rather than a file this run loads, because
  /// Cove has no way to load a module at run time: a package is resolved,
  /// checked, and linked before anything executes. So `--program` names one of
  /// the transformations this package declares, and adding one is a change to
  /// this enum and a `match` arm that the checker will not let anybody forget.
  export enum Program
    case RevenueSummary
    case ConfirmedBookings
    case RateCard
    /// The columns this transformation's output carries, in order.
    export fn columns(self) -> Array<String>
    /// The name `--program` selects this transformation with.
    export fn name(self) -> String
    /// The format this transformation reads.
    export fn reads(self) -> Format
    /// What this transformation does, in one line, for `--help`.
    export fn summary(self) -> String
    /// The format this transformation writes when nothing says otherwise.
    ///
    /// A default rather than a requirement: every transformation's output is a
    /// row of cells, and a cell renders in either format, so `--output-format`
    /// may always override this.
    export fn writes(self) -> Format
  /// What the rate-card transformation carries between records.
  ///
  /// Only whether the header has gone past. A CSV file names its columns on its
  /// first line, and a reader that is handed one line at a time has to remember
  /// that it has seen it.
  export struct RateCard
    field seenHeader: Bool
    field rows: Int
  /// What a revenue summary accumulates.
  ///
  /// One entry per property, and nothing else: the bookings themselves are read,
  /// counted, and dropped, so what this holds is bounded by how many properties
  /// the input mentions rather than by how long the input is.
  export struct Revenue
    field properties: Map<String, Totals>
  /// The empty state a run starts from.
  export fn emptyConfirmed() -> NoState
  /// The empty state a run starts from.
  export fn emptyRateCard() -> RateCard
  /// The empty summary a run starts from.
  export fn emptyRevenue() -> Revenue
  /// Writes nothing at the end, because everything was written on the way
  /// through.
  export fn finishConfirmed(state: NoState) -> Array<Array<Cell>>
  /// Writes nothing at the end: every row went out as it was read.
  export fn finishRateCard(state: RateCard) -> Array<Array<Cell>>
  /// Writes one row per property, in ascending order by name.
  ///
  /// The order is the `Map`'s own, which is ascending by key, so two runs over
  /// the same input produce the same file and a golden test is possible.
  export fn finishRevenue(state: Revenue) -> Array<Array<Cell>>
  /// Keeps one record when it is confirmed, and writes it out at once.
  export fn foldConfirmed(state: NoState, line: String, number: Int) -> Result<Step<NoState>, Detail>
  /// Reads one CSV line, checking the header and normalizing every row after
  /// it.
  export fn foldRateCard(state: RateCard, line: String, number: Int) -> Result<Step<RateCard>, Detail>
  /// Folds one JSON Lines record into the summary.
  ///
  /// A cancelled booking is read and then ignored. It is not an error -- a
  /// cancellation is an ordinary thing for a booking to be -- and it is not
  /// revenue either, so the count it does not join is the count of bookings that
  /// earned something.
  export fn foldRevenue(state: Revenue, line: String, number: Int) -> Result<Step<Revenue>, Detail>
  /// Reads a transformation by name, or reports the ones there are.
  export fn programNamed(name: String) -> Result<Program, Error>
  /// Every transformation this package declares, in the order `--help` lists
  /// them.
  export fn programs() -> Array<Program>

module cq.records
  /// A booking, as this program requires one to be.
  ///
  /// Every field is required and every field has a type. That is the point of
  /// the type: past this struct nothing in the program has to ask whether
  /// `nights` was a number, and nothing has to decide what to do when it was
  /// not. The decision is made once, here, where the record is still next to the
  /// line it came from.
  export struct Booking
    field id: String
    field guest: String
    field property: String
    field checkIn: String
    field nights: Int
    field guests: Int
    field rate: Float
    field status: Status
    field channel: String
    /// What this booking is worth, which is its nightly rate for every night of
    /// it.
    export fn revenue(self) -> Float
  /// What a booking's `status` field may say.
  ///
  /// An unrecognized status is an error rather than a case, because a status
  /// this program has never heard of is a fact about the input that the program
  /// should report rather than average.
  export enum Status
    case Confirmed
    case Pending
    case Cancelled
    /// The word this status is written with, which is the word it was read
    /// from.
    export fn name(self) -> String
  /// Reads a booking out of one parsed record.
  ///
  /// The column is 1 for every failure here, and that is a limitation rather
  /// than a choice: a `Json` value has forgotten where in the line it was
  /// written, so the most this can say is which record was wrong and which field
  /// of it. Carrying a span on every value is what a diagnostic layer would do,
  /// and this program does not have one.
  export fn bookingFrom(record: Json) -> Result<Booking, Detail>

module cq.rows
  /// One value in an output row.
  ///
  /// A row is not an array of strings, because the two formats this program
  /// writes disagree about what a string is: CSV has only text, and JSON Lines
  /// distinguishes `3` from `"3"`. Deciding that once per value, here, is what
  /// lets one program's output go out in either format without the program
  /// knowing which.
  export enum Cell
    case Text(String)
    case Count(Int)
    case Decimal(Float, Int)
  /// A format this program writes.
  export enum Format
    case Jsonl
    case Csv
    /// The name the command line selects this format with.
    export fn name(self) -> String
  /// What one record produced: the state it left behind, and the rows to write
  /// for it now.
  ///
  /// This is the one shape every transformation's step answers in, and it is
  /// what lets an aggregation and a filter be the same kind of thing. An
  /// aggregation returns no rows until its input runs out and everything it
  /// knows is in the state; a filter returns a row per record it keeps and
  /// carries almost nothing. The engine writes whatever comes back at once, so a
  /// filter over a hundred thousand records never holds more than one row.
  export struct Step<S>
    field state: S
    field rows: Array<Array<Cell>>
  /// Reads a format by name, or reports the two there are.
  export fn formatNamed(name: String) -> Result<Format, Error>
  /// The header line `format` starts a file with, if it has one.
  ///
  /// JSON Lines has no header: every record carries its own field names, so a
  /// first line naming them would be a record that is not one.
  export fn header(format: Format, columns: Array<String>) -> Option<String>
  /// Renders one row in `format`, under the column names `columns`.
  ///
  /// CSV names its columns once, in a header the caller writes; JSON Lines names
  /// them on every record, which is why the column names are needed here and not
  /// only there.
  export fn renderRow(format: Format, columns: Array<String>, cells: Array<Cell>) -> String

module hello
  /// Returns a greeting for `name`.
  export fn greeting(name: String) -> String
  /// Runs the command-line program.
  export fn main(args: Array<String>) -> Result<Unit, Error>
    requires console

module httpstatus
  /// HTTP status codes this package recognizes, derived from
  /// `files/status_codes.txt` by `codegen.statusCodes`.
  export enum StatusCode
    case Ok
    case Created
    case NoContent
    case BadRequest
    case Unauthorized
    case Forbidden
    case NotFound
    case Conflict
    case UnprocessableEntity
    case InternalServerError
    case ServiceUnavailable
    /// The numeric HTTP status code.
    export fn code(self) -> Int

module life
  /// Runs one simulation and reports what happened in it.
  export fn main() -> Result<Unit, Error>
    requires console, files, process

module life.forager
  /// The one intent this forager answers the tick with.
  export fn decide(view: SelfView, observation: Observation) -> Decision

module life.instinct
  /// The open cell furthest from `target`, if the creature can step at all.
  export fn away(target: Cell, observation: Observation) -> Option<Heading>
  /// The nearest of these sightings, and the lowest id among those tied.
  ///
  /// A fold rather than a sort: one answer is wanted and a sort would build a
  /// whole ordering to take the front of it. The comparison is strict, so the
  /// earlier element wins a tie -- and `Observation.nearby` already arrives
  /// nearest first and lowest id first, which is the order this preserves
  /// rather than a second ordering laid over it.
  export fn nearest(sightings: Array<Sighting>) -> Option<Sighting>
  /// The cells this creature could step onto: on the grid, and empty.
  export fn open(observation: Observation) -> Array<Patch>
  /// The creatures this one would eat, if it ate creatures.
  export fn prey(sightings: Array<Sighting>) -> Array<Sighting>
  /// The open cell with the most food, if any of them holds any.
  export fn richest(observation: Observation) -> Option<Patch>
  /// The open shelter nearest this creature, if it can see one.
  export fn shelter(observation: Observation) -> Option<Heading>
  /// Turns a heading into a move, and no heading into a rest.
  export fn stepOr(heading: Option<Heading>, fallback: Decision) -> Decision
  /// The predators this creature can see.
  export fn threats(sightings: Array<Sighting>) -> Array<Sighting>
  /// The open cell nearest `target`, if the creature can step at all.
  export fn towards(target: Cell, observation: Observation) -> Option<Heading>
  /// A step chosen by nothing in particular, or a rest when there is none.
  ///
  /// "Nothing in particular" still has to be the same nothing on every run, so
  /// it is the creature's own id and the tick that choose, and not a draw the
  /// behaviour has no generator to make.
  export fn wander(view: SelfView, observation: Observation) -> Decision

module life.predator
  /// The one intent this predator answers the tick with.
  export fn decide(view: SelfView, observation: Observation) -> Decision

module life.rng
  /// A draw: the number that came out, and the generator to draw from next.
  export struct Roll
    field seed: Int
    field value: Int
  /// The next state of a linear congruential generator.
  ///
  /// The multiplier and the modulus are the ones `rand()` was specified with,
  /// and the arithmetic stays well inside `Int`. That matters in Cove, where
  /// overflow is a broken invariant rather than a wrapped result: a generator
  /// that relied on wrapping would stop the run instead of wrapping.
  export fn next(seed: Int) -> Int
  /// A number in `0..<bound`, and the generator to draw from next.
  ///
  /// The high bits are what is kept. The low bits of this recurrence cycle
  /// far too visibly to be a coordinate -- the last bit alternates -- and a
  /// world laid out from them would stripe.
  export fn roll(seed: Int, bound: Int) -> Roll

module life.scavenger
  /// The one intent this scavenger answers the tick with.
  export fn decide(view: SelfView, observation: Observation) -> Decision

module life.schema
  /// What the world did with an intent.
  ///
  /// Every case but the last is something that happened. `Refused` is the
  /// world declining an intent it will not carry out -- a step off the edge, a
  /// meal in an empty cell, a hunt of a creature that is not there -- and it
  /// costs the creature that tick and nothing else.
  export enum ActionResult
    case Moved(Heading)
    case Blocked(Heading)
    case Ate(Int)
    case Hunted(Int)
    case Missed(Int)
    case Hid
    case Rested
    case Refused(String)
    /// The word this result is written with.
    export fn name(self) -> String
    /// Why the world refused this intent, for a result that is a refusal.
    export fn refusal(self) -> Option<String>
  /// A place in the grid, and also a step from one place to another.
  ///
  /// One type for both because a step is what the difference of two places is,
  /// and a second struct with the same two fields would only make the addition
  /// need a conversion.
  export struct Cell
    field x: Int
    field y: Int
  /// The one intent a behaviour answers a tick with.
  ///
  /// Exactly one, whatever the creature would rather do. A behaviour that wants
  /// to move and eat has to decide which, and the world resolves what it said
  /// rather than what it meant.
  export enum Decision
    case Move(Heading)
    case Eat
    case Hunt(Int)
    case Hide
    case Rest
    /// The word this decision is written with.
    export fn name(self) -> String
  /// The four directions a step may take.
  export enum Heading
    case North
    case East
    case South
    case West
    /// The word this heading is written with.
    export fn name(self) -> String
    /// The step this heading is.
    export fn step(self) -> Cell
  /// Everything a creature is told about the world this tick.
  ///
  /// It is bounded: four patches, and at most `sightLimit()` sightings, nearest
  /// first. A behaviour that wants to see further cannot, which is what makes
  /// the cost of a tick a function of the population and not of its square.
  export struct Observation
    field tick: Int
    field here: Int
    field shelter: Bool
    field around: Array<Patch>
    field nearby: Array<Sighting>
    field scent: Option<Heading>
  /// One of the four cells a creature could step onto.
  export struct Patch
    field heading: Heading
    field at: Cell
    field food: Int
    field shelter: Bool
    field outside: Bool
    field occupied: Bool
  /// What a creature is told about itself.
  export struct SelfView
    field id: Int
    field species: Species
    field at: Cell
    field energy: Int
    field hidden: Bool
  /// Another creature, as this one can see it.
  ///
  /// `away` is the number of steps between the two, so a behaviour never has to
  /// compute a distance and two behaviours cannot compute it differently.
  export struct Sighting
    field id: Int
    field species: Species
    field at: Cell
    field away: Int
  /// Which kind of creature this is.
  export enum Species
    case Forager
    case Predator
    case Scavenger
    /// Whether a predator will hunt this species.
    export fn isPrey(self) -> Bool
    /// The word this species is written with.
    export fn name(self) -> String
  /// Every heading, in the order a tie is broken in.
  ///
  /// The order is north, east, south, west, and it is written down here rather
  /// than left to each behaviour, because two species that broke a tie
  /// differently would make the same run depend on which one moved first.
  export fn headings() -> Array<Heading>
  /// How many sightings an observation carries, at most.
  export fn sightLimit() -> Int
  /// How far a creature of this species can see, in steps.
  ///
  /// The predator's is the long one, and it is what makes a predator a
  /// predator: prey walks away from what it can see, so a hunter that saw no
  /// further than its prey could only ever find one by walking into it. It is
  /// still bounded, and so is what it can be told about what it sees.
  export fn sightRange(species: Species) -> Int
  /// Whether this species can smell food it cannot see.
  export fn smells(species: Species) -> Bool
  /// The distance between two cells, in steps.
  export fn stepsBetween(from: Cell, to: Cell) -> Int

module life.world
  /// What is alive, what it is standing on, and what has happened so far.
  export struct Census
    field tick: Int
    field alive: Int
    field foragers: Int
    field predators: Int
    field scavengers: Int
    field food: Int
    field energy: Int
    field births: Int
    field deaths: Int
    field refusals: Int
  /// One creature, as the world keeps it.
  export struct Creature
    field id: Int
    field species: Species
    field at: Cell
    field energy: Int
    field hidden: Bool
    field born: Int
  /// One creature's intent for this tick.
  export struct Intent
    field id: Int
    field decision: Decision
  /// What one creature's intent came to.
  export struct Outcome
    field id: Int
    field species: Species
    field decision: Decision
    field result: ActionResult
  /// The world after a tick, and what every intent came to in it.
  export struct Turn
    field world: World
    field outcomes: Array<Outcome>
  /// Everything there is, at one tick.
  export struct World
    field tick: Int
    field seed: Int
    field width: Int
    field height: Int
    field food: Array<Int>
    field creatures: Array<Creature>
    field nextId: Int
    field births: Int
    field deaths: Int
    field refusals: Int
  /// The world one tick later, and what every creature's intent came to.
  export fn advance(world: World) -> Turn
  /// The most creatures of one species this world holds at once, per cell.
  ///
  /// A cap rather than a curve, for two reasons. A simulation that can double
  /// its population twice is a simulation whose running time nobody has
  /// bounded, and this one is run by a test. And a cap per species is what
  /// keeps a predator boom from being the last thing that happens here: a
  /// predator population that cannot grow past a fortieth of the grid can take
  /// the foragers down and cannot take them out, so the world goes on having
  /// all three species in it.
  export fn capacity(species: Species, cells: Int) -> Int
  /// Which cell of the grid this is.
  export fn cellIndex(world: World, at: Cell) -> Int
  /// The census of this world.
  export fn census(world: World) -> Census
  /// The creature with this id, if it is alive.
  export fn creatureNamed(world: World, id: Int) -> Option<Creature>
  /// One intent per creature, in creature-id order.
  ///
  /// A `map`: every creature is asked the same question about a world none of
  /// them has changed yet, so the answers cannot depend on each other and the
  /// order they are computed in is not a fact about the run.
  export fn decisions(world: World) -> Array<Intent>
  /// How much food this cell holds.
  export fn foodAt(world: World, at: Cell) -> Int
  /// The state hash: one number that is the whole world.
  ///
  /// Two runs of the same seed and the same number of ticks agree here or the
  /// simulation is not deterministic. It is a `fold` because that is what a
  /// hash is -- every element, in order, into one accumulator -- and the
  /// arithmetic stays inside `Int`, where overflow would stop the run.
  export fn hash(world: World) -> Int
  /// Whether this cell is on the grid at all.
  export fn inside(world: World, at: Cell) -> Bool
  /// Whether this cell is a thicket: a place to hide, and a place no hunt
  /// reaches into.
  ///
  /// This is the refuge, and a world without one does not last. A predator and
  /// its prey both move one cell a tick, so prey that can be seen can always be
  /// caught eventually, and a run with nowhere safe ends with the predators
  /// eating everything and then starving in an empty world. It ended that way
  /// for every seed until the thickets were here.
  ///
  /// Derived from the coordinates rather than stored, because a thicket never
  /// moves and a second array would be a second thing to keep in step.
  export fn isShelter(at: Cell) -> Bool
  /// The most food one cell can hold.
  export fn maxFood() -> Int
  /// The world a seed describes, before anything has happened in it.
  export fn newWorld(seed: Int, width: Int, height: Int) -> World
  /// How many creatures of one species are alive.
  export fn population(world: World, species: Species) -> Int
  /// Carries out the intents, in creature-id order, and answers the world they
  /// leave behind.
  ///
  /// It takes the intents rather than asking for them so that a test can hand
  /// it intents no species would produce. That is how this package says what it
  /// means by isolation: an intent the world will not carry out costs the
  /// creature that made it its turn, and the loop goes on to the next creature.
  export fn resolve(world: World, intents: Array<Intent>) -> Turn
  /// The world one tick later.
  export fn tick(world: World) -> World

module restricted
  /// Reads only through the document capability supplied by the host.
  ///
  /// `console` is reached only through `text.report`, so this module requires
  /// the console capability without naming a host module for it.
  export fn main() -> Result<Unit, Error>
    requires console, documents

module server
  /// JSON body returned by the health endpoint.
  export struct HealthResponse
    field status: String
  /// Returns a stable health response without external I/O.
  export fn health(request: http.Request) -> http.Response
    requires http
  /// Runs the HTTP server.
  ///
  /// The loop belongs to the program rather than to the host: `handle` answers
  /// one request and returns, so the run's fuel, deadline, and cancellation
  /// reach a server exactly as they reach any other Cove code. It ends when the
  /// listener has nothing more to serve.
  export fn main() -> Result<Unit, Error>
    requires console, http

module tasks
  /// Data needed to render the dashboard.
  export struct Dashboard
    field bookings: String
    field prices: String
  /// Loads independent dashboard inputs concurrently.
  ///
  /// The two fetches run on threads of their own, and `clock.timeout` bounds the
  /// wait for both together: a body it stops does not finish, and the error
  /// names the bound rather than whatever the stopped body was doing.
  export async fn loadDashboard() -> Result<Dashboard, Error>
    requires clock, http

module text
  /// Reports the word count of `text` on the console the host granted.
  export fn report(text: String) -> Result<Unit, Error>
    requires console
  /// Counts words in `text`.
  export fn wordCount(text: String) -> Int

module traits
  /// A room booking.
  export struct Booking
    field id: Int
    field guests: Int
    conforms traits.Summary
    /// Returns the line this value takes in a report, which defaults to its
    /// summary as an ordinary bullet.
    export fn line(self) -> String
    /// Returns the one-line summary of this value.
    export fn summarize(self) -> String
  /// A payment recorded against a booking.
  export struct Receipt
    field bookingId: Int
    field cents: Int
    conforms traits.Summary
    /// Returns the line this value takes in a report, which defaults to its
    /// summary as an ordinary bullet.
    export fn line(self) -> String
    /// Returns the one-line summary of this value.
    export fn summarize(self) -> String
  /// A value that can summarise itself for a human-readable report.
  export trait Summary
    fn summarize(self) -> String
    fn line(self) -> String (default)
  /// Headlines one entry.
  ///
  /// The bound is checked at the call site, which is also where `T` is chosen,
  /// so `summarize` resolves to exactly one implementation. That is why this
  /// function takes one entry rather than a mixed collection: every value it
  /// sees has the same type.
  export fn headline<T: Summary>(entry: T) -> String
    capability-open
  /// Prints a report built both ways.
  export fn main() -> Result<Unit, Error>
    requires console
    capability-open
  /// Renders a report of entries whose types may differ.
  ///
  /// `dyn Summary` values carry their implementation, so `line` is resolved
  /// from each value rather than from the signature. That is what lets one
  /// array hold a `Booking` and a `Receipt` at once.
  export fn report(entries: Array<dyn Summary>) -> String
    capability-open

module values
  /// Completed immutable booking data.
  export struct Booking
    field status: BookingStatus
    field guests: Array<String>
  /// A value whose scalar field copies and whose Vector field shares storage.
  export struct BookingDraft
    field status: BookingStatus
    field guests: Vector<String>
  /// Lifecycle state of a booking.
  export enum BookingStatus
    case Pending
    case Confirmed
  /// Exercises Cove's value copies, Vector aliases, and freeze transition.
  export fn main() -> Result<Unit, Error>
    requires console
